summary: 1. High-stayed videos (38.7%-45.8%) get straight to a high-contrast physical contradiction in the very first 4 words without conversational filler like 'Ever wondered' or 'You've seen'. 2. Top-performing titles pose direct, short tension-driven questions ('Why Don't Planets Fall Into The Sun?') rather than academic textbook labels with subtitles ('How Colour Vision Works: The Biology of...'). 3. Shorter video durations under 36 seconds significantly correlate with higher stayed percentages compared to 38-57 second videos. 4. Videos about intuitive physical mechanics (space gravity, optics) dramatically outperform abstract microscopic biology (vaccines, cone cells). 5. Hooks asking 'Why don't we crash?' create immediate existential stakes, whereas passive open-ended questions ('How do vaccines train...?') fail to retain initial swipers.
winning_hooks: If the Sun pulls the Earth, why don't we just crash into it?
Why does baking soda fizz the moment it hits vinegar?
Have you ever noticed that a magnifying glass can make things look huge, but pull it away and the world flips upside down?
avoid: Conversational fluff openings: 'Ever wondered...', 'You've used soap your whole life...'
Academic titles containing secondary descriptors like 'The chemistry of...' or 'explained'
Durations over 37 seconds that dilute the core payoff
Generic explanation questions lacking conflict, like 'How do vaccines actually train your immune system?'
next_experiment: Test Hook Velocity: Compare a 30-second script starting immediately with a high-stakes contradiction ('If heavy objects fall at the same speed, why does a feather drift?') against an opening stating 'You've seen objects fall...'
